segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Good morning and welcome to the University’s Open Day and to our mini-lecture from the Sports Studies department.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now the purpose of this lecture is twofold: one — we want you to experience a university lecture, to give you a taste of what listening to a university lecture is like, and two — we want you to find out something about the Sports Studies program at this university.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So feel free to ask any questions during the talk and I’ll do my best to answer them.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Right — so what does a course in Sports Studies involve?

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Well, you wouldn’t be blamed for not knowing the answer to this question because Sports Studies as a discipline is still comparatively new.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: But it’s a growing area and one which is now firmly established at our university.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now there are three distinct strands to Sports Studies and you would need to choose fairly early on just which direction you wanted to follow.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: And I’ll just run over these now.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Firstly, we’ve got the Sports Psychology strand, secondly, we’ve got the Sports Management strand, and last, but not least, there’s the Sports Physiology strand.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So Just to recap there’s Sports Psychology, Sports Management, and Sports Physiology.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Let’s look first at Psychology.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now the people who study Sports Psych want to work with top athletes, and they’re looking at what will take those athletes that one percent extra.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: What makes them win?

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: When all other things are equal, physically all other things are equal, they want to know … what are the mental factors involved?

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: The Sports Psychologist works closely with the athlete through his or her training program and becomes an integral part of the team.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: In fact you could say that they play just as important a role as the coach.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So if you’re interested in what makes people win this could be the area for you.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now secondly, we’ve got the strand which I referred to as Sports Management and this goes hand in hand with the area of Sports Marketing.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So you might like to think of this area as having two branches: Management and Marketing.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: On the Management side we look at issues relating to the running of sports clubs, management of athletes that sort of thing.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: But then on the other side, we’ve got Sports Marketing.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: And this is the side that interests me more because here we will look at the market forces behind sport.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Questions like: why do people spend their money on a football match, or a tennis game rather, than say on buying a CD or going to the cinema?

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: What are those market forces?

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Sport used to just compete with sport.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Nowadays it competes with other leisure activities.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: The spectators go to sport to be entertained rather than out of loyalty to a team.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: They want to have an evening out and they don’t want the cheap seats any more they want good seats they want entertainment.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: And the professional sportsmen and women respond to this without question.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: They’re there to give a performance.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: They provide the entertainment.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So in the marketing course we address all these commercial issues and we look at how this hooks back into the Management of sport.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now the third branch of Sports Studies sometimes comes under another name and is also known as Exercise Science.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: And again here we find that there are two distinct types of exercise science.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: The first is working very much at the macro level.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: What I call the huffing and puffing people.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So this looks at fitness testing, body measurements, all that sort of thing.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: But the more interesting side of sports physiology, at least in my view, is the side that looks at the micro level, looking at cellular change.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: They’re doing cellular research, looking at changes in body cells when the body is under stress.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: So that just about brings us to the end of our mini-lecture for today.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: I hope you’ve found it interesting and I look forward to seeing you all on our course next year.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Feel free to come and talk to me if you want any more information.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: I’ll be over at that notice board near the main entrance.
